blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how not-for-profit organisations like charities manage their finances without focusing on profit?

blocks.markdown: Not-for-profit organisations operate differently from profit-oriented businesses. Their main goal is to provide services rather than earn profit. Understanding their financial statements is crucial for effective management.

blocks.title: Receipts and Payments Account
blocks.text: A receipts and payments account is a summary of cash transactions over a period, showing all cash received and paid, regardless of the period they relate to.

blocks.markdown: Unlike a receipts and payments account, an income and expenditure account is similar to a profit and loss account. It matches income earned during a period against the expenses incurred to determine surplus or deficit.

blocks.title: Accumulated Fund
blocks.text: The accumulated fund represents the net assets of a not-for-profit organisation at the beginning of a period. It is similar to the capital in a profit-oriented business.

blocks.title: Calculating the Accumulated Fund
blocks.prompt: Calculate the accumulated fund given the following: Assets at the beginning of the year are ₦500,000, and liabilities are ₦150,000.

steps.text: Identify the total assets at the beginning of the year.
Identify the total liabilities at the beginning of the year.
Subtract liabilities from assets to find the accumulated fund.

blocks.markdown: Subscriptions can be in arrears or in advance. Subscriptions in arrears are amounts due but not yet received, while subscriptions in advance are amounts received for future periods.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always distinguish between receipts and payments accounts and income and expenditure accounts by focusing on the timing and nature of transactions.

points: Receipts and payments accounts summarize cash transactions without considering the period.
Income and expenditure accounts match income with expenses to determine surplus or deficit.
The accumulated fund is similar to capital in profit-oriented businesses.
